title: Smooth approximation of a Lipschitz function with almost-everywhere convergent derivatives (mollification, parent step (3.2)(iii))
statement: Let k ∈ ℕ, L ≥ 0 and let g : ℝ^k → ℝ (ℝ^k = Eucl k) be L-Lipschitz. Then there are functions G_m : ℝ^k → ℝ (m ∈ ℕ) such that: every G_m is C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞), i.e. smooth of every finite order, not analytic); every G_m is L-Lipschitz; G_m → g uniformly on ℝ^k; and for Lebesgue-a.e. w ∈ ℝ^k, fderiv ℝ G_m w → fderiv ℝ g w in ℝ^k →L[ℝ] ℝ as m → ∞ (fderiv ℝ g w is the Fréchet derivative, 0 where g is not differentiable).
lean_statement: ∀ (k : ℕ) (L : ℝ≥0) (g : Eucl k → ℝ), LipschitzWith L g → ∃ G : ℕ → Eucl k → ℝ, (∀ m, ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) (G m)) ∧ (∀ m, LipschitzWith L (G m)) ∧ TendstoUniformly G g atTop ∧ ∀ᵐ w ∂(volume : Measure (Eucl k)), Tendsto (fun m => fderiv ℝ (G m) w) atTop (𝓝 (fderiv ℝ g w))
